topics.why_in_news: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation released the 27th edition of 'Women and Men in India 2025' highlighting gender indicators related to health, education, employment and governance.
prelims_quick_notes: Published by Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI).
Uses data from Census, NFHS, PLFS and SRS.
Female Labour Force Participation Rate increased in rural areas.
Gender parity achieved at school education level.
Gender budgeting introduced in India in 2005-06.
key_findings_and_indicators: Sex Ratio at Birth improved from 904 to 917.
Rural Female LFPR increased from 37.5% to 45.9%.
Female Gross Enrolment Ratio in higher education increased to 30.2.
Women in managerial roles recorded major growth.
Improvement observed in gender parity indicators.
Metadata added for 50 indicators improving statistical transparency.
important_facts: MoSPI publishes Women and Men in India report.
LFPR includes employed and job-seeking population.
GER measures enrolment relative to eligible population.
Articles 14, 15(3) and 16 support gender equality framework.
SDG-5 focuses on gender equality and women empowerment.
Gender Budgeting institutionalised in India from 2005-06.
exam_relevance: Important for Social Justice, Governance and Human Development.
Useful for gender equality, inclusive development and demographic dividend topics.
Can be linked with women empowerment, labour participation and SDGs.
prelims_traps: Women and Men in India report is published by MoSPI, not Ministry of Women and Child Development.
LFPR includes both employed and unemployed persons seeking work.
GER indicates enrolment, not actual attendance.
Sex Ratio at Birth differs from overall Census sex ratio.
